hint: alarms.holidays, the holidays option of alarms and the beforeRing event in scripts need AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} (internal build {{ required_host_version_code }}) or later and this plugin 1.2.0 or later; with plugin 1.1.x or earlier, calls fail with a message asking to update the plugin

Holidays and makeup workdays are only as accurate as the upstream data (the open source project python-holidays); years not yet announced are estimated by rule and marked "estimated", and are corrected by a data update once announced
feature: Holidays: alarms get the options "Skip holidays", "Only on holidays" and "Only on workdays" (rings on every workday, makeup workdays included, never on weekends or holidays); holiday data for 250 countries and regions (with more than 600 subdivisions) from 2020 to 2035 is built in, with the makeup workdays of mainland China and Taiwan

The settings screen chooses the default holiday region (first taken from the system region), and each alarm can use its own region; the alarm list shows how many holidays the next ring skips; estimated years are marked "estimated", as days off and makeup workdays may still change

Holiday data is checked for updates every week (can be turned off on the settings screen; metered networks are not used by default) and can be checked by hand on the settings screen; downloaded data is signature checked and the current data stays in use when the check fails; in a year without data an alarm rings by its repeat rule alone and is never silenced for that reason

Decided by a script before the ring (beforeRing): a registered script is started before the ring (60 seconds by default, 15 seconds to 5 minutes) and can skip this ring, or let it ring with a different label, sound, spoken text or vibration this time only; when the script does not decide in time, fails or AutoJs6 is unavailable, the alarm rings as usual

New in the AutoJs6 script module: alarms.holidays (list regions, tell holidays and workdays, list a year's holidays, show and refresh the data), the holidays option of alarms, skip / ring of the beforeRing event, and warnings in alarms.capabilities() about missing data and estimated years (needs AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }}; see the [AutoJs6 documentation](https://docs.autojs6.com/#/alarms))

New plugin tool holiday_check tells through the MCP Server plugin or plugins.tools.call whether a day is a holiday or a workday in a region and the holiday's name; alarm_add and alarm_update accept the holidays option

hint: alarms.timers and alarms.stopwatch in scripts need AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} (internal build {{ required_host_version_code }}) or later and this plugin 1.1.0 or later; with plugin 1.0.x the calls fail with a message asking to update the plugin
feature: Timers: up to 20 timers at once, with a preset length (1 minute to 1 hour) or a custom one (1 second to 100 hours) and an optional label; timers can be paused, resumed, extended by 1 minute and reset, and ring like alarms when they end

A running timer shows its countdown in the notification shade, where it can be paused, extended by 1 minute or cancelled; timers keep counting after a reboot, and a timer that ended while the device was off rings after the boot (if it is more than 5 minutes overdue, only a missed notification is left)

Stopwatch: start, pause, resume and reset, up to 100 laps, with the fastest and the slowest lap marked; while it runs it shows in the notification shade, which can be turned off in the "Timers and stopwatch" group of the settings
The bottom navigation switches between the alarms, timers and stopwatch pages

New alarms.timers and alarms.stopwatch in the AutoJs6 script module (needs AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }}): starting, querying, pausing, resuming, adding or removing time, resetting and cancelling timers, scripts registered for a timer to start on ring and other events, and controlling the stopwatch with laps (see [AutoJs6 documentation](https://docs.autojs6.com/#/alarms))
New plugin tools timer_start, timer_list and timer_control to start, list, pause, resume, extend, reset and cancel timers through the MCP Server plugin or plugins.tools.call
System clock: timer requests are handled too; other apps can have the plugin start a timer, open the timers page or dismiss a ringing timer

fix: When another app or an AutoJs6 script sent two alarm requests of the same kind in quick succession (for example two new alarms in a row, or two calls of alarms.system.setAlarm aimed at this plugin) while no plugin screen was open, the second request was ignored without any message and its alarm was never created; every request is now handled; on Android 7.0 - 8.1 this needs the "reorder running apps" permission (granted at install)

hint: Enabling the plugin in the Plugin Center, the plugin tools and the alarms script module need AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} (internal build {{ required_host_version_code }}) or later; with older AutoJs6 versions (for example 6.8.0) the plugin works only as a standalone alarm clock app

On ColorOS (OPPO, OnePlus, realme), turn on auto launch for the plugin in both the app details and Settings > Apps > Auto launch, otherwise alarms do not ring once the plugin process has been cleaned up (see README > FAQ)
feature: Alarms: one-time or repeating alarms with RFC 5545 calendar rules (weekdays, the nth weekday of a month, the end of a month, day intervals, end dates and counts); dates can be excluded, or only the next ring skipped

Ringing: a system ringtone or imported local audio, spoken text, independent volume with a fade-in, custom vibration, snooze and auto silence, a full screen ringing screen on the lock screen, and alarms due at the same time ringing one after another

Scheduling: alarms are rescheduled after a reboot, a time or time zone change and a plugin update, ring before the first unlock, and a missed alarm rings within 5 minutes or else leaves a notification
Plugin screens: alarm list, edit screen, ringing screen, permissions page and settings; language, night mode and theme color follow AutoJs6 by default, and the launcher icon can be switched

Settings: default ringtone, vibration, snooze and auto silence, time format, automatic update checks, and the optional "Keep running in background" (a silent notification that makes cleanup by the system less likely)

The permissions page checks notifications, exact alarms, full screen alerts, battery optimization, background restrictions and the vendor's auto start one by one, with extra guide rows for the auto launch list and banner notifications on ColorOS

AutoJs6 script module alarms / $alarms (needs AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }}, Rhino only): adding, querying, changing and removing alarms, event listeners, scripts registered for AutoJs6 to start when an event happens, and the ringtone list (see [AutoJs6 documentation](https://docs.autojs6.com/#/alarms))

Plugin tools alarm_add, alarm_list, alarm_update, alarm_remove, alarm_set_enabled, alarm_skip_next, alarm_upcoming, alarm_dismiss and alarm_snooze, callable through the MCP Server plugin or plugins.tools.call
System clock: handles the set, show, dismiss and snooze alarm requests of other apps
A single APK for every device, including devices with 16 KB memory pages
dependency: Attach lib-recur 0.17.1 (calculates the repeat rules of alarms)
Attach Desugar JDK Libs 2.1.5 (date and time zone calculations on Android 7.x)
